chapter: Today's music, Coltrane and leading a band
title: Choosing players and the chemistry of a band
summary: Selecting sidemen by human chemistry and humility, with Miles as a master of it.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: What about um...the, the interaction with, with players in the band?

Yeah, I think the, well in addition to, because, certainly, the brass tacks are, are more than a little important, but uh, because that’s another– I, I think of Ellington again, because he had a lot of uh...I mean, he had tonal characters, and , and literal characters [chuckling] in that band. What’s, what’s your experience been, is, is, is there a, is there an art to uh–?
Yeah. Is there an art to keeping that kind of family functioning?
Yeah, I think there is. You have to know the elements. It’s having a knowledge of, of human chemistry in selecting the group.

Um some people work well together, some don’t, for different reasons. They have to be on a level of kindred sensibilities, in terms of aesthetic interpretation, presentation. Like Kenneth Brand[?] used to say, “We don’t need ‘tudes,” meaning “attitudes.”

[chuckling] They don’t work, you know. So, you had to be humble, and, and willing to work together, in spite of having ability, and sensibilities. And Miles was, he was, more or less, a genius at putting together groups that worked.
